utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness gave evidence of the shelling of Sarajevo on the 16th of October. That was a separate issue altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you would say these new dates were in the additional information sheet but have not been used?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, this Chamber does not know anything about it. It is not part of the evidence produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. And my basic point is that my friend's complaint is that he didn't have an opportunity to receive instructions on those dates. He did. They were provided with the translation yesterday, as well as not emerging in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then is the Defence ready to resume cross-examination? Mr. Usher, would you please then bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Colonel Niaz. I again have to apologise. Lawyers always deal with procedural issues and it always takes time. I thank you for your patience. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your patience, sir. Now we shall resume where we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. stopped. Do you know where the command post of this 5th Brigade is located? It is, I think, called the 5th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please show us where this post is located?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This post, the brigade headquarters, 5th Motorised Brigade headquarters was located inside Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, which part of Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The exact location, I would not be able to, but it was on the -- you go inside Dobrinja for about -- exactly, I am not sure but it was definitely in Dobrinja, there is no doubt about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us if you know where the command posts of the battalions of the 5th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Colonel, same question about the command posts of the companies?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. According to your experience, a brigade counts how many men?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, depend upon the armies of various country, but a brigade is normally about 4.000 to 5.000 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Is it true that there were about 10 brigades within Sarajevo while you were staying there?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you the exact count, but the brigade which I understood was -- the headquarters was 5th Motorised Brigade, there was an HVO brigade and there was 102 -- I am not sure. There was three brigades which were -- headquarters which were in my area of operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I am sorry for interrupting you but we are short of time. I am not trying to be impolite. Do you know where the headquarters of the other brigades were located? Could you locate the places where the headquarters of the other brigades were located; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know, does the street name of Benevolencija mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know what MUP is?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: How do you spell this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: M-U-P.

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Colonel, now I would like to speak about your military training, please, and more specifically in connection with your training in the Balkans. You told us yesterday that you had arrived, first of all, in the region of Zagreb. Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You said that you were trained in crater analysis which lasted two hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe two, three hours. Exact --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: From two to three hours, I think that was your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask the witness be allowed to finish his answers when he is clearly responding to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In general terms, we are to allow the witness to, but if there is any specific need to stop the witness, of course, this will be allowed if he would go into an area which is not very relevant for the party that asked the question. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am sorry for interrupting you. It was not what I wanted. I thought that I understood that you had finished your sentence. You said two or three hours of specific training, is that true?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't remember the exact time but this could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Have you completed your answer?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, to the extent that you had had that training, could you, first of all, indicate to the Chamber what you know about theoretical variations of parabolic shots. If you know, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it may be a matter of translation, but the question has not -- does not appear in English in a way which seems to be clear or logical. The witness is being invited to indicate what he knows about theoretical variations of parabolic shots. I don't know what a parabolic shot is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that is especially what Mr. Piletta-Zanin wants to find out. In his view, it means something and he wonders whether the witness would explain what it means. But unless you say it is -- if you don't know what it is, Mr. Ierace, that does not automatically mean that it doesn't mean anything at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I understand that entirely, Mr. President, but the use of the word "parabolic" in that context, I don't know that that could have been intended. A parabola is a particular path. A parabolic shot simply doesn't make sense. I stand to be connected.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The shot as such is not parabolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what you want to say?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: MR. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am very glad that the Prosecution, for the very first time, understands that a shot is not parabolic. It is an excellent point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it possible, Witness, in regard to Markale, that the shot was not a parabolic one, as I think or perhaps the Prosecution has confirmed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's just -- I am afraid that we have now a complete confusion. If I do understand well, is that Mr. Ierace says that not a shot as such but a trajectory of the projectile may be parabolic. I am not saying that it is parabolic, but that is the trajectory rather than the shots that could be parabolic. And he asks to reformulate the question in such a way that this might become clear to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I should add that the witness has not yet given any evidence about whether he conducted a crater analysis of what in the Prosecution case was a mortar shell impact at Markale market.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think what -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin is now testing the level of knowledge after the two to three hours' course. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it is perhaps a difficult question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, have you in your training in Zagreb, were you in any way informed about the possible variations, parabolic variations, when firing both with regard to a 120, 82 and 72 millimetre?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would not be in regard to 120, 82 or 72 millimetre. If I am not wrong, you were referring to the trajectories. That is what you mean by "parabolic"?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am talking about the character, the parabolic nature of the trajectory and its possible practical variations. Were you specifically trained on those matters?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question asked by my friend referred to 120, 82 and 72. I wonder whether my friend meant 62 instead of 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are problems of this kind, that Mr. Ierace should listen to the French because I didn't talk about 62.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you could have asked this question -- because the witness confirmed that, so you could have asked it in re-examination, Mr. Ierace. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a bit perturbed and I will have to dab at my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, was your answer "no," you had no specific training in that regard?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just an orientation training, and if I may correct you, the, calibres of mortar, 120, 81 and 60 millimetre. No 82 and 72.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for clarifying this. Witness, this general orientation intervened in the courses of two or three hours that you had?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because we were just generally to learn, not in specific terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Okay, Witness. Witness, in response to a question of the Prosecution, you said that as a rule there were at least two of you to conduct on-site investigation. Now you have confirmed this. The person who was with you, did the person have the same technical and theoretical training as you?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were in fact on -- you are referring to which place? Which incident are you referring where we had two --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am referring in general. You said, "as a rule, there were at least two to conduct investigations" and that you always had with you a junior officer. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a junior officer in the technical terms but I just had another military observer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The other military observer, Witness, did he have the same training as you?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You never discussed between you about your respective trainings?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, may I correct you here. That training in Zagreb as pertaining to the various military observer was not specific in nature. Now, what matters was the actual experience with the various UNMOs were having from their training and their own particular country.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Specifically, did you know people amongst you who had at least one person who had a complete training of a ballistics expert?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was then not the team leader. But in my team, there was once -- yes, I remember once there was an artillery officer. And the artillery officers are supposed to be expert in crater analysis and all these trajectories. I am an infantry officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Colonel, you said that in one of your teams, you had one artillery officer, which seems a minimum as far as I am concerned. Was that person an expert in ballistics? Did he follow courses in ballistics at the university or at a higher level; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was his training and what was his name, please?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Major Saleh, and he was from Jordan. He was a major, and it is understood that in all professional armies, if a general is reduced to a rank of a major and he is supposed to know, he should have gone through various courses and ballistics --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I have to stop you, I am sorry. That person, that major who was an artillery officer, did he, yes or no, have the status of an expert ballistic expert, that someone can be an expert in law or medicine? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the artillery officers are supposed to be expert in ballistics.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, may I ask you, do you have any specific knowledge about the training, also academic training, of the person you just referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, sir, not in detail.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So this gentleman you have mentioned, Saleh, Major Saleh, did this person carry out investigations with you? Did he carry out on-site investigations together with you?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer, Witness. Witness, I would like to continue on this subject which regards technical matters. Do you know whether it is important or not in order to determine the origin of a shot, is it necessary to find elements that have remained after a shell has been fired and to find these elements intact? Sir, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, as a result, would you agree with me that if it appears that such elements, and I am referring to a stabiliser in particular, if these elements have been moved, sir, taken away and then put back, in such cases, the investigation should be regarded with caution because of such manipulations? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would definitely affect the investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I would like to return to an incident with regard to which you gave testimony, the Markale incident. Do you know that there were about 10 investigations which were carried out in regard -- with regard to this particular incident, with regard to this shelling?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I know, that there were -- during my time, there was only one official investigation carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. I am going to go back to what we spoke about, what we saw a minute ago, and I have to list a certain number of matters. And please answer briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know where the 101st brigade was located?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The 1st Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The 2nd Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The 1st Motorised Brigade --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are developing a speed, and I notice that you referred to speed already before, because moderato is not the way of playing but is a matter of speed, as you know, which cannot be followed by the court reporters or the translators. So I am not asking you to go lento, but a bit slower.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to verify your answer. I was speaking about the 1st, and your answer hasn't entered into the transcript -- the 1st Motorized. And your answer is "no," is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And with regard to the 2nd Motorised?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Same answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you don't know?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: For the 5th, you said somewhere in Dobrinja?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: For the 9th brigade -- thank you. Sir, for the 9th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The 10th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: For the brigade that you yourself mentioned during the examination-in-chief, the so-called Croatian brigade, exactly where was that brigade located?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for that answer. Witness, I will show you a map in a minute. My colleague has made me think of this and I think that it would be a good moment, if the usher could help us, and turn towards us. Witness, we are going to show you some maps, and in order to make things easier, we have made fairly large copies of this map. I am not sure that there are eight copies, but I think that there will be a sufficient number. It is the same map as the one that is usually presented by the Defence but usually we present only one copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I apologise. Usher, would you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, with the help of the usher, could you place this map on the ELMO so that we can all have a look at it. Sir, do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, could you ask for the microphone to be placed a little closer to you. That will avoid problems with the translation. Thank you very much. Sir, do you recognise this as a map of Sarajevo? Could we zoom in? Zoom in toward what the witness is looking at so that we can all see this. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This appears to be distorted map. The locations doesn't appear to be the exact locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Let's adhere to the principal that the map is not as wrong as we might think. On the basis of this map, which is an official one, could you show us precisely where the main positions, the main Lima positions were; do you know?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were not -- we were -- the UNMOs inside the Sarajevo city, the Papa UNMOs were not supposed to be knowing the locations of Lima side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I understand that you weren't supposed to know where the Lima positions were, but were you aware of this fact, at least? If not, just say "no."

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. The general area that from where the confrontation line was passing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. How many Lima positions were there? Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you. We had maybe 8 to 11 OPs in Lima side. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you very rapidly point them out on the map, and use a pen to mark them with the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I was not even -- I don't know where the OPs were located inside the Serbian territory. We never visited those places.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, is it true to say that these posts were, as a rule, situated next to the firing positions of the Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say anything on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it true, as a rule, that according to military practice, observation posts are placed next to places where something is happening and not in locations where nothing at all is happening?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily all the OPs. The observation posts are supposed to be established at location from where they can observe, directly observe, most of the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for this answer. Sir, do you know where the main firing batteries of the Bosnian Serb army were located?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I never visited that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't ask you whether you had visited that place or those places. What I am asking you is whether you had any certain knowledge. If not, just say no.

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this answer. Sir, could you tell me where the pointed rock is located? Colonel, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The translation might be a bit behind and then, of course, the witness cannot answer your question until the translation had the opportunity to be finished. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is quite right, Mr. President. In that case, should I repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question has been translated into English as an inquiry as to where the pointed rock was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think the witness used the term "sharp" though.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was, I said, near Sedrenik. This was --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please give the witness the opportunity to finish the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the question, and it would be fair to the Defence if the objection was heard in his absence. Perhaps I can refer to it obliquely. When a witness is asked to indicate something on a map provided by the party, there are certain things that should be done as a matter of fairness in relation to that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It is still a bit of guessing for me. I don't know whether it is true for the others as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the map -- the exercise should be capable of being carried out in relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can I respond to that very briefly? This witness is a military expert. He said that he needed 24 hours to become a colonel, and I think that if someone knows how to read a map, that should be an infantry specialist. He should be able to do so if he is asked where a position is. People like me, get lost.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection, as far as I understand it, is that if you ask someone to do something, it should be possible for him under the given circumstances to do what you asked him to do. Would you please keep that in mind because we might ask you afterwards whether -- what the situation was in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I should also say, Mr. President, there are two aspects to the map in that regard which are wanting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am going to return to the question that I just asked you. You said on several occasions that shots which came from the centre of the town came from the region which you called the "sharp stone." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, on this map, and given that you stayed for one year in Sarajevo, could you point out where the sharp stone is located? Could you do that?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I correct you? My stay was not one year in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I still object. There is a preliminary question which hasn't been asked, which is: Is that place on this map? Rather than: "Can you point it out" or "Will you point it out." I also at this point indicate quite specifically, since my friend refers to the military background of the witness, that this is a map which also does not have contours. So there are two issues: One, contours, and secondly, whether that place of which we have all heard evidence indeed appears on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think I -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it if you ask the witness to mark a specific or at least to indicate where a specific place is and you give him a map, that at least the place you ask for is within the boundaries of that map. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as it is a mountain, obviously, I gave certain indications to the witness. I don't want to give him indications, but part of the mountains are on the exterior. I have already provided the answer now. We also spoke, and you are aware of this, Mr. President, of the seven forests area, and this area appears quite clearly in this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you point out the area of the seven forests, please?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, you never heard the seven forests area being mentioned?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a bit -- it is a tourist map, basically. We are not used to tourist maps as far as my training is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, do you know which army was located - and perhaps I will put that in the plural - which armies were located in the Sedrenik area?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the Serbian army. The Serbian army was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, Witness, I am asking you the following question: Which armies were located in the area that I have just mentioned, the Sedrenik area? And if there was only one there, tell me which one was there.

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on both sides of the confrontation lines, on the inside side were the Bosnian and the other side were the Serbians. But I have not been on the exact confrontation line in this area because this area used to be very, very dangerous for us to go. Rather, most of the time, we were told not to go in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your answer, sir. Sir, would I be correct if I said that in this area which was especially dangerous, there were two active fronts: One was that of the Bosnian Serb army and the other front was the BH army, the so-called BH army front. Is that exact?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for that answer. Do you know whether there was any fighting in this area and whether this occurred on a frequent basis?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Frequently, sir?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, a while ago you said that, as a general rule, when you would speak about the shells that had hit the centre area, that they came from that direction. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, did you yourself carry out on-site investigations of these -- of the traces of these shells, if there were any such traces?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in some cases, but in --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Colonel, in how many cases? Could you please answer that?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you are talking to the cases which were -- which I referred to in the near vicinity of the marketplace --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Exactly, sir.

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be five, six.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, in these cases, you indicated the general direction?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, what enables you to say and to claim categorically today before this Trial Chamber that a shell didn't come from that direction which came from one of the armies or perhaps from the other army?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps I can help my friend at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With pleasure. With pleasure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I was careful in examination-in-chief to ask the witness as to the direction rather than the point of origin. The question asked by my friend seemed to go beyond that but perhaps I could assist him by saying I don't seek to go beyond the direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That is one of the questions that came into my mind, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. You asked: What enabled the witness to say and to claim categorically today that a shell didn't come from that direction, I think that the question was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, to be brief, I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I think that you understood the question. When you carried out investigations of these six -- these five or six cases, what enables you to say, since the two armies were positioned in that area and there was fighting, what enables you to say, with precision, that the shots came from one army rather than from another army?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before the witness answers that question, I will try again. Perhaps I can do it a different way. I will not --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...point in dispute. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I listened carefully to the line of questioning of Mr. Ierace, and he stopped when we talked about direction. And as far as I understand Mr. Ierace, that it is not the position of the Prosecution, it is not part of the case of the Prosecution, that in those specific cases that this witness would have drawn any conclusions in respect of the spot from where the fire --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, can I point out the following: You noticed that my questions are sometimes articulated, not always, but sometimes. Some questions depend on each other. And to the question that was put to this witness by the Prosecution, the witness denied that there were shots which may have come from a Muslim side. And I am trying to question the witness's credibility in such a case what enables him to affirm categorically that, in theoretical terms, there was not a shot fired from one of the armies, namely, from the Muslim army? And I think it is quite normal for me to put this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What line are you referring to if you say that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to the witness's reply, I think it was yesterday. I can verify that. I will verify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I could help. It was the case yesterday that I asked the witness whether, in relation to any of the analysis he did, he was able to establish that the source of fire was within the confrontation lines, and he replied that he was not able to make that conclusion. But I am trying to help my friend. If he goes to today's transcript, the English version, page 63, line 24, he quite clearly linked this question to the crater analysis done on the impacts in the area of Markale. Now, perhaps I can approach it this way: I will not be seeking to argue that this witness's evidence establishes a point of origin of the mortar impacts which he analysed within a radius of 200 metres of Markale, only the direction of the trajectory. If one looks at the questions that my friend has asked this witness, at the line I have indicated and thereafter, he is clearly questioning this witnesses about the point of impact in relation to those particular mortar impacts. I invite my friend to not pursue it but to stay with the direction and not the point of origin. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...take more time to discuss these kind of issues. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I will let you proceed for the time being, as long as there is no misrepresentation of the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, please put your question again and I will listen carefully whether there is any misrepresentation of the testimony of the witness, and please keep also in mind that the Prosecution does not seek to establish through this witness that whatever the direction may have been, that this would make it possible for us to establish the point from where the shell was fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I shall bear all of that in mind. But I think that it is important for us to ask the right questions at the right time and to the right witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, you said in response to a question asked by the Prosecution that, as far as you knew, not a single mortar shell fell in the interior of the city of Sarajevo, not a single shell from the -- fell in the interior from the BH army side; is that correct? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as per my knowledge. I would like to clarify the Honourable Judges regarding a thing, that the UNMOs on the Lima side and the Papa side were on the wireless communication. So immediately, if a round was fired from the Serbian side, it was immediately reported upon and vehicle also headed. Similarly, if a round was going out from the Bosnian sides, and vehicle -- we were -- a particular OP would pass it on the radio set, and similarly, the rounds coming in, we would report it. So in most of these --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I respectfully interrupt. I think it appropriate to go into closed session in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to know why because we are wasting a lot of time like this. May I know why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...kept in mind specifically by myself, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, but we are not going to ask Mr. Ierace to explain the reasons because I do understand that he wants to explain the reasons in the absence of the witness. Mr. Niaz, I have to ask you to leave the courtroom just for one moment. Mr. Usher, would you please accompany Mr. Niaz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Just for the transcript, I would like to say in line 75, 12, says: "It was immediately reported upon and was heard," something like that. That was what the witness said. "Immediately heard," something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if you would just grant me 30 seconds. Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, I proofed this witness and during that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it is in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I take it we are in closed session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we are not, as a matter of fact. You didn't ask -- did you ask for closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise. Let me just look to see if we need any redaction until now. I don't think that you said anything up to this moment that would need a redaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That is so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then could we turn into closed session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Niaz, I hate to -- please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hate to tell you same apologies, same reasons.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, we shall continue. Are you aware of the fact that in Sarajevo during the period that you stayed there, were you aware of the fact that there were mobile targets?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mobile targets for which army?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am talking about Sarajevo, the interior, that is to say, either of the so-called Bosnian army, the governmental Bosnian army, or perhaps of the HVO army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the question. My friend should indicate more specifically what he means by the words "mobile targets."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness would not understand that question, then he would certainly inform us. Please proceed. You may answer the question, Mr. Niaz.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One were the human targets when we were moving and the second were the UNMO vehicles, the -- my vehicle was shot. So I don't know, that was a target.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am talking about military targets, legitimate military targets. That is to say, do you have any knowledge of tanks in Sarajevo, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any tank in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, sir. Did you see, during your one-year stay in Sarajevo, any vehicles, any cars, which were transformed in order to make it possible to transport mortars or to make it possible to transport devices for firing shells?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see such vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the -- it might be misunderstood. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, did I understand you well that you said that these vehicles were transformed in order to make it possible to transport mortars or to fire mortars? The transcript says, "to transport mortars or to make it possible to transport devices for firing shells."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President, to have mentioned that. That was my question. But I have difficulty in seeing the screen tonight. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, does this affect your reply in any way? Does this change your answer?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't see such vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, during your stay in Sarajevo, did you see any vehicles which were armoured, which were initially civilian vehicles but which had been provided with armour in order to transform them into military vehicles?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't remember. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for this answer. Now, sir, on several occasions you said that there was shelling on civilian towns. Do you remember mentioning this?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not civilian towns. I said in there was shelling in the city, in the central part of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have a problem, it seems, of translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I said of a civilian character, you are right, Witness, but I would like to follow me. Targets of a military nature. I think the term you used was "civilian area." Is that what you remember?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a civilian area and the civilian casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, the first thing I would like to ask is: How can you claim that these were civilian targets if you didn't know where all the various control and command posts were located, the ones which I mentioned a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If bombs land in a house and there are no military installation or any mobile target nearby, and it kills the civilians around, so it is obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, you say that it is obvious. Do you regard this as an established fact that we know that in Sarajevo there was a certain number of military targets of a mobile nature? We know that you haven't seen them, but how can you be certain, how can you claim categorically in the testimony that you have been giving that there were no mobile military targets next to the places that you have mentioned, the places that you said were of a civilian nature?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I didn't see any such mobile target for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, the simple fact that you did not see them, does that fact exclude the possibility that they were perhaps present there?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they could be present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. When you say that civilian targets were fired at, are you referring in general to the situation such as you knew it or in particular to incidents which you investigated?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in particular to the incident which I investigated because, as I mentioned earlier, that one of my tasks at the end of the day, daily, was to go to the morgue and the Kosevo hospital to investigate or to see for myself the casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, how can you exclude the fact that there were no troops, perhaps no soldiers, in such-and-such a place that you might have visited after the explosion?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot determine that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Witness, do you know whether it is true - and we have testimony to this effect - that in the vicinity of Markale, there was police post which was -- which consisted of 60 or 65 men, between 60 and 65 policeman? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The most of the police station which I had visited, none of them was having such a large number. But I don't remember police post near the Markale marketplace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know where Drvarska Street is located?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know if there were other police posts in the Markale area?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in the -- the one police station which I can directly remember in my area was Pofalici police station. It was a little far away from the Markale.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, a while ago you spoke about civilian victims in response to a question that was put to you. Is it true, Witness, that a large part of the armed forces in Sarajevo didn't have a complete -- didn't have complete uniforms? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Do you know whether women were also combatants?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was some women in the army, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer, sir. When you are shown the body in the morgue which might be the body of a woman and which doesn't have a uniform, and doesn't have any wounds, on the basis of seeing this body, what allows you to claim that it is the body of a civilian or a member -- or of a member of the military?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you right, I mentioned that the day, it was a rotation day. The weekend was a rotation day, and once I ask my interpreter why there is so much of a rush here today in the marketplace. He said that in this day, on this day, the soldiers come from the front line to exchange their cigarettes for the food stuff. So you are right in saying that there could be possibility and there must be also certain soldiers in civilian clothes being part of that massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. But my question didn't have to do with this massacre in general. You said that one of your missions consisted of going to verify the presence of bodies in the morgue; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, when you are shown a body in the morgue - and I am not speaking about Markale; I am speaking in general - when you are shown a body which doesn't have a uniform and which might be the body of a woman, how can you categorically exclude that this isn't a loss which happened in fighting, perhaps at the front line?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some of this cases, it could have been as you say. But in most of the cases, it was related to a bomb which had landed at a certain place from where the casualties were evacuated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. Have I understood your correctly when saying that on the basis of seeing the body in the morgue and as a general rule, on the basis of seeing the body, nothing would allow you to state whether this was the body of a soldier or of a civilian?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said, not in all cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer, sir. I would like to continue with this question relating to shellings and shots. Sir, do you know whether it is true - and we have testimony to this effect - that very young children below the age which is usually accepted as combatants were taken in by the BH army in order to carry weapons, bear weapons?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact -- do you know whether there were very young children in Sarajevo carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see, but one thing for sure. I had visited almost this entire front of Sarajevo on my area of operation. I didn't come across a single child, not a single child. That is for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, for this answer. I know that you are an officer, not an artillery officer but an infantry officer, but I would appreciate it if you could provide me with a technical answer. We think that we know that when there are artillery shots, when mortar shells are fired, technique requires -- because of technical reasons, the target is not hit by the first shot, there is a long shot and then a short shot and afterwards you attain the target; is that correct? Could you confirm this principle?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This principle is known as "bracketing," and you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, is it true - because we have had testimony to this effect - that what we as the Defence call the "margin of error" is roughly in the region of 300 metres, a diameter of 300 metres -- or, rather, an area of 150 metres?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally, the artillery target or the mortar target is an area target, and an area target, it could be a little more also.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I remind you, I did some computing on time. It was not easy this time. But I deduct all the time in closed session and all the debate we had before. There would remain another five minutes. Another five minutes would then remain.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I will bear that in mind, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would now like to address the question of shelling. Can you confirm, because we have also received testimony to this effect, could you confirm that when a mortar shell is fired, the effect is fairly silent, it doesn't produce a loud noise?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as compared with the artillery. The mortar -- yes. But you can't say it is silent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I said "fairly."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we please -- no, I will consult my colleague.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know whether there were also sniper units in the BH army?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You said that you had also carried out an investigation into sniper incidents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And you said that you would often base yourself on the investigations that had been carried out by the local police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, our investigation, we would not officially report it unless it was confirmed by UNMOs. So if a report was given by a local policeman, we would add with the word "confirmed by UNMO." That would mean that we were sure to agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you, Witness. One other question, Witness: Do you know what the 7th Brigade was?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you earlier. It could be a brigade. I did not visit the headquarters of this brigade, neither was I aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I asked whether you knew what it was. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, if I tell you that this brigade was composed of mujahedin, were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of any mujahedin brigade in Sarajevo at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were you aware of any mujahedin brigades outside Sarajevo, perhaps in Mount Igman, in the Igman mountain?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only -- I have not seen it, but I heard that there was a brigade operating in some central Bosnian location. I am sorry, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you talk about a brigade, are you talking about a mujahedin brigade?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what the question you asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And my very last question: How could you claim, since you yourself had not seen the shots, that the incidents in question was sniper incidents since fighting was going on, and one is well aware of the danger that stray bullets represent?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as sniping is concerned, I said earlier that I was myself sniped at while I was taking a civilian old woman from the sniper alley, probably wounded then. The vehicle was -- my vehicle was sniped at. The very fact that Sarajevo city itself contained large number of these container vehicles, the trams, located at the place where the civilian could crawl safely. The very fact was that one could hear lot of sniping activity going on continuously inside the city. And most of the sniping was done by a 12.7. So the wound made by a 12.7, it is little more severe or more vital than a bullet at maybe in the confrontation line like when they are fighting with 12.7, a smaller calibre, where there could be a stray bullet coming in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this information. I have to interrupt you. I have another three short question. The first one is: Do you know whether the BH forces also had a 12.7 calibre weapon?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once I reviewed the heavy weapons. There was one anti-aircraft gun which I remember taking it out, but I don't remember at this moment whether it was 12.7 or some -- I don't remember the calibre. But it was definitely one light anti-aircraft gun which I --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will interrupt you. The 12.7 that you have mentioned, was that an anti-aircraft rifle, what one calls a triple-A gun, or was it a personal weapon?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12.7 is basically an anti-aircraft gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, do you know -- do you know the Zrak factory? Say "yes" or "no," if you can?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Could you tell us in which circumstances you remember the date of the 16th of October, which you yourself corrected quite recently, that is to say, in the course of this month?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will need initial testimony or the initial investigating team which came to my country, then I didn't bring my diary along. So I may have missed the month, but the date was very, very clear in my mind. So the second time, probably two years back, when I was again asked to give a written statement from my country, on that day, I consulted my diary. And I have my diary with me here. It says the 16th of October. And if you see the diary, you can find that it cannot be a fabricated one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That is not necessary, Witness. That is not necessary. But could you please just tell me, since the incident we have spoken about, the shelling of the town was an incident that affected you, why didn't you speak about this in the course of your first examination?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are talking about 16th of October?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am talking about the incident in which two women were allegedly hit by a mortar shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the questions asked by my friend indicate some confusion, at least in the English translation. The evidence of the witness in relation to the 16th of October was that the city received in excess of 1500 or 2000 shells. There was another incident where a woman and a child were shelled. The witness has not said that the incident involving the woman and child happened on the 16th of October.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I didn't mention a date with regard to this incident. I only mentioned the incident in which these two women were targeted by a shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, why didn't you mention this fact at your first examination?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are referring to the first testimony or -- not the testimony, the first investigation report?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I am talking about your written statement which was submitted a few years ago, I think you said, submitted to Mr. Jan Van Ecke and to Mr. Asif Akhtar Syed?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are right. That investigation was basically regarding the Markale market.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But why didn't you mention this fact, Witness, can you tell me?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told them there was a lot of sniping activity. If they asked me to quote a particular incident, I would have done it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, Witness, since you could have done it, I have one last question: The site where this shelling occurred, was it an open space where it was possible to see everything or was it an enclosed space in the city?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was a street, smaller street, a narrower street than the bigger street, but it was not so narrow that I couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you took now 10 minutes, and you said that this was the very last question. So this is really the last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: As a result, Witness, you weren't able to know whether in one or the other of the parallel streets there was a military objective; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace. Is there any need to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked whether you came across children carrying weapons and you replied: "I didn't come across a single child." Did you mean by that, that you did not come across a single child carrying a weapon or that you never saw children in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw large number of children in Sarajevo, but none with a weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you were asked questions about how you could tell if a casualty in the hospital was a civilian or not. When you visited the hospitals daily to check on the casualty figures, did you ever have an interpreter with you?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Always.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to the wounded patients?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever ask them what their occupation was?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did that ever assist you in determining whether or not the shelling victim or sniping victim was, in fact, a civilian?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is one of the major fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked whether -- you were asked some questions about the sound that mortars make when they are fired and you said that they were not as loud as artillery. What about different size mortars? In other words, are you aware as to whether the firing of 120-millimetre mortar makes more sound or less sound or the same sound as, say, a 62-millimetre mortar?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is 60-millimetre mortar, not 62. Definitely the calibre is different and the sound is different.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When a mortar is fired, is there a range of charges that can be placed underneath the shell?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does the sound differ, according to the number of charges placed under the shell?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe. I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. In that case, I won't ask you any more questions about that topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked questions as to whether you were able to determine if a mobile target had been present near the site of shellings in Sarajevo. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I think you were then asked as to possible mobile targets, whether you had seen any tanks in the city, and you said you had not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What were some of the places of impact of shellings that you investigated? In other words, what type of places were they?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the places which I investigated were, let's -- were places where I couldn't find any military target. For like Kosevo hospital, shelling inside the city or centre area, Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I think one target you mentioned at one point during cross-examination was a house. You were explaining how you could tell if a target was a civilian target or not, and I think you gave an example of a house which contained civilians and no military equipment. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Approximately how many shelling incidents that you visited involved shelling of houses?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A number of them. Well, this particular incident I am referring was it was in the city that -- the center city, and it was a direct hit inside an apartment where the inhabitants were living.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many of the shelling sites you investigated involved not just houses but buildings of whatever description?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the buildings -- most of the buildings were inside the city, the high buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you able to assist us with an approximation of the percentage of shelling incidents that you investigated where the site of the shell impact was a building of some description or another?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is very difficult to at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. If you can't do it, that is all right. When you questioned surviving victims, did you ever ask them whether there were any military weapons nearby or equipment or soldiers at the time that the shell impacted?

utterances.speaker: AFZAAL NIAZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but if at times you used to visit that place and see for ourself that were there any -- like the incident I specifically quoted in my testimony about the Kosevo hospital shelling. In that particular incident, I, along with my team members, we search the complete area of.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Since the Bench has no further questions to you, this concludes your testimony given in this court. I thank you very much for having come the long way to The Hague. I also especially thank you for the patience you showed when we were dealing with other matters and I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you please escort Colonel Niaz out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you assist us in the paperwork.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D112, map marked by witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but was it finally marked? It was intended to be marked but no marks were put on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. Well, can it be returned to us? What is important is that the witness could not write anything into the map, so that we will take it back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For our witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the time is too short to start with the examination of the next witness but let me just, for another reason, confer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The parties should prepare for the trial to resume tomorrow as scheduled normally. So at this very moment, a request for a one-day delay is denied. As the Chamber indicated before, if we find that there is any need for further time to prepare for cross-examination, we will also determine how much that time would be. But it is our experience that it can be better assessed very often once we know the problem and when we have heard the examination-in-chief. So, therefore, we will start with the next witness to be examined in chief tomorrow in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I thank you for your decision. We will take note of it. And the Defence will clearly state that it is not in a position to start its cross-examination tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber has taken notice of this observation. If there is nothing else for this moment to be discussed, then we will adjourn until tomorrow, quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
